cards.key: Luka Doncic is out, so Collin Sexton and Sandro Mamukelashvili and Austin Reaves should play more than usual.
Jalen Duren is out, so Cade Cunningham and Kevin Huerter and Daniss Jenkins and Ausar Thompson and John Collins and Paul Reed should play more than usual.
Dennis Schroder and Brandon Miller are out, so Royce O'Neale and Christian Anderson and Grayson Allen and Coby White should play more than usual.
Kawhi Leonard is out, so Jamal Shead and Trayce Jackson-Davis and Allen Graves and Ja'Kobe Walter and RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles should play more than usual.
Tyrese Haliburton is out, so Quenton Jackson and Larry Nance and Andrew Nembhard and Jarace Walker and Jalen Slawson and Aaron Nesmith should play more than usual.
Clint Capela is out, so Alperen Sengun and Tari Eason and Jabari Smith should play more than usual.
Victor Wembanyama has the top projection in this game at 51.0 DK points.

outs.note: The show said Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. That removes a bench guard from the Charlotte rotation.

The show said Brandon Miller is out for Monday's game with a hip strain and that no long-term timeline has been announced. He played only 14 minutes in his last game on November 6. Charlotte is running very thin on healthy players.

benefits.note: Show: more minutes if Miller misses time (11/07)

outs.note: The show said Merrill is already ruled out for Nov. 9 against Charlotte. He played 13 minutes on Nov. 6 and did not play on Nov. 7.
The show said Tyson is already ruled out for Nov. 9. He has not appeared in a Cleveland box score since Oct. 29.

Doncic sat on Nov. 8 at Detroit with low back tightness. The show assumed he plays the second leg of the back-to-back against Atlanta on Nov. 9 but noted the back issue left no posted total for that game. The show said he is about 70 DraftKings points per game this year (the box scores show about 67 per game) and that Atlanta's defenders do not matter against him at $12,000.

benefits.note: 30 minutes, 13 points, 8 rebounds when Doncic sat (10/28)

outs.note: The show said Tyrese Haliburton should still be out for Indiana on Monday. He has not played since October 26.
Leonard has not played since October 23. The show said it does not know whether he will be back in week 4.

benefits.note: 6+ assists in each of last five games off the bench, 20 to 25 minutes (11/04)
Show: could see a few more minutes, not far past 20 (10/28)

outs.note: Capela started on Oct. 30 with Alperen Sengun and Steven Adams out, but he is now out himself. He missed Nov. 2 with a right ankle sprain.

injuries.text: Allen left after 7 minutes on Nov. 4 and missed the Nov. 6 and Nov. 7 games. The show treated him as uncertain for Nov. 9 and said Evan Mobley becomes more interesting if Allen is out again, though it called Mobley a boring play who does not shoot more when others sit.

Quentin Grimes started for the resting Luka Doncic on Nov 8 and had 12 points and 4 assists in 32 minutes. He hurt his finger late, did not return, and had negative X-rays, so the show said there is some doubt he plays on Nov 9. The show said he does little when Doncic plays.
Tyler Herro hurt his knee on Nov 8 but returned to the game, finishing with 13 points in 27 minutes. The show called it his first bad game of the season.

Show: large usage bump in limited minutes (11/06)

log: Aaron Gordon was given a double technical in the fourth quarter against Golden State on Oct. 26 and exited the court. He had seven points. He played 25 minutes.
The show said Aaron Nesmith is slowly ramping up. He started and played 30 minutes Sunday against Brooklyn with 11 points.
Aaron Nesmith returned to the starting lineup Wednesday at Memphis and scored 16 points in 30 minutes, including the late three that sealed the win.
Aaron Nesmith averaged about 24 minutes, 13 points and one steal over his last seven games. The show said minutes limits have held him back, but he played 30 minutes in each of his last two games.
Aaron Wiggins has scored in double figures in all six of Atlanta's games this season while coming off the bench. He has done it with hot 3-point shooting and very few free-throw attempts.
Aaron Wiggins played 24 minutes off the bench on November 2 and scored seven points. He has played 23 or 24 minutes in each of his last four games.
Aaron Wiggins has come off the bench in every game and played 29 minutes Wednesday with Jalen Johnson out, scoring 15 points. His value comes mostly from points.

Aaron Wiggins played 29 minutes off the bench on November 6 and scored 19 points with 3 threes. The show said he bounces between a low-end starter and a streamer, and it noted that Atlanta is entering a very light stretch of its schedule.
Aaron Wiggins scored 20 points with 4 rebounds, 6 assists and a steal in 26 minutes off the bench. The show said he took 19 shots and got hot late in the game.

Ace Bailey remains a Utah starter, but his recent production has dipped with 20.0 and 21.5 DraftKings points in his last two games. The show said his role could shrink further once Lauri Markkanen and especially Jaren Jackson Jr. are both back.
Ace Bailey started and played 32 minutes on Nov 8 but scored only 7 points, with 4 steals saving his line. The show said he is only a must-roster player because of Utah's injuries.
Aday Mara is getting more playing time off the bench with Chet Holmgren out. He has played 20 to 28 minutes in each of his last four games, including 10 points and nine rebounds Monday.

Mara's minutes have climbed since Chet Holmgren went down, going from 12 to 14 minutes early in the season to 28 on October 31, 20 on November 2 and 25 on November 4. He made his first start on November 4 against Cleveland, and the show said that was likely because the Thunder went big to match the Cavaliers' double-big lineup. The show said his usage rate has fallen from about 20 in the preseason to about 16, and it expects 21 to 25 minutes a night with strong block numbers.

Aday Mara played only 18 minutes off the bench on November 6 against Memphis after playing more against Cleveland's two-center lineup. The show said his minutes are not guaranteed and depend on facing a big opponent where he can share the floor with Isaiah Hartenstein.

Aday Mara started and played 27 minutes on November 7, posting 18 points, 8 rebounds and 3 blocks, after playing 18 minutes off the bench on November 6. The show said that since Chet Holmgren went down it expects Mara to average around 22 to 23 minutes, and it noted the Thunder's center rotation is hard to predict game to game.
Adem Bona played 25 minutes on Oct. 25 the last time Philadelphia started Dean Wade with LeBron James at center. He could see a bigger role Saturday if James and Jabari Walker are unavailable.
Adem Bona started Saturday with Joel Embiid resting and played 22 minutes. The show said he is a blocks option whenever Embiid sits a back-to-back.

Adem Bona has been out since Nov. 4 and was ruled out on Nov. 8 with a cervical spine sprain. The show said he is a block streamer if he returns, especially if Joel Embiid misses games. Embiid has played every recent game, including 29 minutes on Nov. 8.
AJ Dybantsa played 27, 30 and 33 minutes in his first three games, and the show said his minutes limit keeps rising. He scored 21 points Monday while Alex Sarr was out.
AJ Dybantsa had nine points, six rebounds and three assists in 32 minutes on November 4. The show said he carried a 28% usage rate in his first two games back.
The show said AJ Dybantsa is off his minutes restriction. He has played 30, 33 and 32 minutes in his last three games.

Dybantsa scored 19 of Washington's 75 points at Oklahoma City on Nov. 7 after playing 36 minutes on Nov. 6. The show said he has not broken out in the two games without Anthony Davis and it would prefer Davis to be out before playing him at $6,600.

Green has played 20 to 24 minutes off the bench in each of Milwaukee's last four games. Gary Trent Jr. has played only once in that stretch, for 6 minutes on Oct 31. The show said Green is mainly a three-point source.
Ajay Mitchell had six points and a steal in 26 minutes Saturday after early foul trouble.
He had 20 points, five rebounds and a block in 35 minutes as a starter Monday. The show expects him to keep the role because no returning player is likely to take his job.
Mitchell has started every game since Oct. 26 and played 32 to 35 minutes in his last two games, scoring 20 and 23 points. The show said Alex Caruso's return should not cut into his role much.
Ajay Mitchell scored 35 points in 30 minutes on November 6. The show said he is set for a big run with Oklahoma City dealing with long-term injuries, which include Chet Holmgren's 8-10 week absence.
Horford played Sunday but came off the bench for 9 points and 5 rebounds in 22 minutes. The show expects him to sit Monday.
Al Horford played 18 minutes on Thursday, and he has played 17 to 22 minutes in every game this season.
Al Horford sat Monday, Nov. 2, for rest on the second night of a back-to-back, not an injury, and is available Thursday.
Alex Caruso returned from injury on Wednesday and played 20 minutes off the bench.

Caruso returned on Nov. 4 after missing four games and played 20 minutes off the bench with seven points. The show said he should carve out his own role with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams likely out for the season and Chet Holmgren sidelined.

Alex Caruso played 20 minutes off the bench on November 6 in a blowout win. The show said about 20 minutes is enough for him to have value, that close games are his best path to more minutes, and that he might rest on back-to-backs.

Alex Caruso had four total steals and two total blocks in his first five games while averaging 19.2 minutes off the bench. He scored in single digits in four of those five games, and the show said Oklahoma City keeps limiting his minutes.

Alex Morales, a two-way player, played 14 minutes on November 2 after not playing on November 1, and he played 9 and 7 minutes in the two games before that. He has been part of the rotation with Jalen Suggs out.
He is questionable with left knee soreness, and Deandre Ayton started at center in his place Monday and played 24 minutes.

With Anthony Davis out on November 6, Deandre Ayton started at center, but Alex Sarr played 30 minutes and posted 13 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 steals and 2 blocks. The show said Sarr became the de facto big man because Ayton is not very good, and it noted that his line came specifically because Davis sat.

The show said Sarr's usage rate has dropped from about 25 to 16 and his minutes from 27 to about 25 per game with Anthony Davis now in Washington. The show also said his blocks are down from two per game to about one. He had a 3-point game in 29 minutes on October 30 and then missed Washington's November 2 game, which the show suggested may mean he was playing through something.
Sarr had 15 points and 14 rebounds on Nov. 7 with Anthony Davis out. The show said Sarr is an easy click at center on Nov. 9 if Davis sits, but that he has less upside when Davis plays.

Alijah Martin had a career game with 27 points, 6 threes, 2 steals and a block in 31 minutes off the bench. He had not played more than 16 minutes in any earlier game this season. The show said it does not buy the performance unless Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley stay out.
He sat Wednesday with low back soreness, and Steven Adams (calf) and Marcus Smart (forearm) were also out. Fred VanVleet scored 24 as Houston moved to 5-0.
Alperen Sengun is questionable tonight at Dallas with low back soreness after sitting Wednesday. Fred VanVleet scored 24 with Sengun out and is off the report for the first night of a back-to-back.
He missed Friday with low back soreness, and Clint Capela started at center with 11 rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes. Houston has not posted its injury report for Saturday yet.
Alperen Sengun played 39 minutes on Wednesday and had a triple-double with 17 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists. The show said Houston has been limiting minutes for most of its other players.
Alperen Sengun had 15 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists and a block in 32 minutes. The show said he looked a little passive as he comes back from an injury.
Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama at the rim to win Houston's game against San Antonio on Oct. 23. He had 20 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks.
He played 39 minutes at Dallas on Friday and had 15 points and six assists.
He had 14 points in 25 minutes Monday. The show said he is the one Rocket who looks out of sync in the current lineup.

Amen Thompson played 32 minutes on Wednesday with 11 points and one assist, after playing 28 and 25 minutes in his two previous games. The show said his assists are down and his minutes are lower than last season.

Amen Thompson is averaging 32.6 minutes after leading the league in minutes last season, and the show said his per-36 production is nearly the same. The show said his assist rate is down with more offense running through Alperen Sengun and Fred VanVleet back, and his block rate has been cut in half.
Amen Thompson played 39 minutes on November 7 and had 17 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks. The show said his lower usage this season has kept his production below last year's level.
He returned Wednesday and had 18 points and 14 assists in 35 minutes, and he runs the offense with Haliburton out.
He had 22 points, nine assists and five three-pointers in 30 minutes Friday at Miami. His production is boosted while Tyrese Haliburton is out.
The show said Andrew Nembhard's usage has been very high since Tyrese Haliburton went down. He had 23 points, four assists and four three-pointers in 35 minutes Sunday against Brooklyn.

Andrew Nembhard is averaging 18.5 points and 7.3 assists in about 33 minutes, and the show said his usage is well above its projection with Tyrese Haliburton out. In the three games without Haliburton since October 28, Nembhard has averaged 21 points, 9 assists and about 39 DraftKings points, compared with about 28 DraftKings points in the three games they played together.
Andrew Nembhard returned to the lineup Wednesday at Memphis and scored 22 points in 38 minutes.

Andrew Nembhard played 31 minutes with 9 points and 8 assists as a starter on November 7. The show said he is playing heavy minutes and getting assists while Haliburton is out, but his efficiency and assist pace are likely to cool.

Andrew Wiggins is struggling, and his minutes have come down to 24 on November 2 and 23 on November 4. The show noted Miami has played Pelle Larsson ahead of him while Klay Thompson's minutes have risen.
Andrew Wiggins had three points and four rebounds in 23 minutes on Wednesday, and the show said he can probably be dropped.

Wiggins started but played only 21 minutes and scored two points on Thursday at Golden State. The show said there is no real role for him and that Pelle Larsson is playing more because Miami needs floor spacing around Giannis Antetokounmpo.
Wiggins started but played only 21 minutes Thursday and had 2 points, 6 rebounds and 4 assists. The show said his usage was about 15 percent and he is not fitting well with Giannis Antetokounmpo.
Andrew Wiggins moved to the bench on Nov 8 but still played 32 minutes because Pelle Larsson was in foul trouble. He had only 6 points and 3 rebounds.
Anfernee Simons should get more shots if Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and LeBron James sit. He scored 21 points with five 3-pointers in 31 minutes off the bench Friday.
Anfernee Simons has been productive off the 76ers' bench, scoring 20, 21, and 19 points in his last three games. He hit five or more threes in each of those games.

Anfernee Simons scored 20, 21 and 19 points with 16 combined 3-pointers in three straight games from Oct. 28 to Oct. 31. He then fell to six points Monday and zero points in 10 minutes Wednesday off the bench.

The show said Anthony Black's production is boosted while Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs are out. Black is averaging 16.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 4.8 assists with about 33.4 DraftKings points per game, including 31 and 33 minutes in his last two games.
Anthony Black started for Orlando on Nov. 5 and had 10 points, seven rebounds and six assists in 31 minutes. He has started four of his five games this season while Jalen Suggs is out.

Anthony Black is starting with Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs both out, and he played 38 minutes for 51 DraftKings points on Nov. 7. The show doubted he keeps this production once Banchero and Suggs return.
He is questionable Friday at Atlanta with an ankle sprain that he played through Wednesday, when he scored 50.5 DraftKings points.
He missed Friday with his ankle sprain, and the show doubts he plays both games of the back-to-back that continues Saturday at Oklahoma City.

Davis missed Washington's games on Nov. 6 and Nov. 7, and the show treated him as questionable again for Nov. 9 against Detroit. In his last three games played he scored 47.75, 45.75 and 50.5 DraftKings points, and the show said he should not be under $9,000 if he plays.

He has missed two straight games with his ankle sprain and is questionable again at Detroit. Kyshawn George scored 33 and 38.25 DK points in the two games without him, and the show expects George to be the most popular play if Davis sits.
Anthony Edwards is expected to miss about two months after knee surgery on Oct. 29.
The show said Asa Newell would get more playing time if Jalen Johnson sits, and he could be a candidate to start. Newell played 19 minutes off the bench on Oct. 31 with 13 points.

The show said Asa Newell is dealing with a toe issue and that Jock Landale may be returning. Newell has missed Atlanta's last two games, and Landale has not played since October 31. If both sit, the show named Zuby Ejiofor, who has played 15 to 18 minutes in his last three games, as a deep-league stream.
Ausar Thompson's minutes have been held down by an early injury, foul trouble, and a blowout. He played 33 minutes in the opener but has not topped 29 minutes since.

Ausar Thompson's steals and blocks are down to about 1.6 steals and 0.8 blocks per 36 minutes, from roughly 2.7 to 2.8 steals per 36 over the past two seasons. The show expects those numbers to rise and noted he is playing more minutes.

Ausar Thompson played 34 minutes on Nov. 4 with 11 points and 17 rebounds, and he played 33 minutes on opening night. The show said his minutes are up about two per game from last season, though he played only 26 minutes in two lopsided games.
Ausar Thompson is averaging 4.7 assists, one steal and 0.6 blocks over seven games. The show said his rebounding is up partly because Jalen Duren is out and may drop when Duren returns.

Thompson started but played only 24 minutes on Nov. 8 while Daniss Jenkins was hot, finishing with 7 points and 11 rebounds. The show said he is good whenever he gets extended minutes but often loses time to foul trouble and blowouts.
Reaves played 39 minutes Sunday against Toronto and scored 19 points; the starters had to come back in the final minutes after Toronto cut a 16-point lead to five.
Austin Reaves scored 25 points in 38 minutes Friday against Portland.

Reaves scored 43 points with 5 rebounds and 4 assists in 37 minutes on Nov. 8 with Luka Doncic out. The show said he will be the highest-rostered player on Nov. 9 if Doncic sits, but it would avoid him at $8,000 if Doncic plays because he has not shown a ceiling next to Doncic.
Ayo Dosunmu started and scored 26 points in 39 minutes Friday at New Orleans.

Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points with 4 threes and 2 steals in 30 minutes as a starter on Nov 8. The show said his starting role comes from Anthony Edwards' long absence and that he is a top-50 fantasy player so far. Minnesota has a two-game week.
Baba Miller played 20 minutes as the backup center on Nov 8 with Isaiah Jackson and Yanic Konan Niederhauser out. He had 12 points, 5 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals and 2 blocks.

He had 16 points, nine rebounds, two steals and two blocks in 31 minutes Monday. The show said his usage is down to about 21.7 percent from about 25 percent last season and that his steal rate is likely to fall.
Bam Adebayo has scored at least 40 DraftKings points in four straight games. He posted 35 points and 10 rebounds for 57 DraftKings points in 41 minutes Wednesday.
Adebayo had 18 points and 10 rebounds in 33 minutes on Thursday at Golden State. The show said his usage is much lower this season and that he has cut down on three-point attempts.
He started Monday with Paul George out and had 11 points, five rebounds and three made threes in 27 minutes.
Baylor Scheierman played 29 minutes off the bench on Wednesday with Jayson Tatum out and Payton Pritchard leaving early, posting nine points and 11 rebounds.
Ben Sheppard is having surgery Wednesday to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee.
Ben Simmons is out for the season.
Mathurin played only 7 minutes on Nov 6 and has not topped 19 minutes in his last four games. The show said New Orleans has too many players for him to get steady minutes.
The show said Stirtz started the second half for the Thunder on Nov. 4. He played 22 minutes off the bench with 16 points and four threes.

Washington started Deandre Ayton on Nov. 6 and then started Coulibaly over Ayton on Nov. 7, when Ayton played only 7 minutes. Neither move worked, since Coulibaly scored 0 points on Nov. 7 and the show called both games horrendous.
The Clippers signed Blake Wesley to a 10-day contract using a hardship exception because of their injuries.
Bobby Portis is playing a bench role for Miami, but his minutes have dipped from 24 on October 26 to 18 on Monday.

Bobby Portis played 21 to 27 bench minutes in most early games, but he has played 17 or 18 minutes in his last three. He scored 25.5 DraftKings points with 10 rebounds and 5 assists in 18 minutes Wednesday.
Portis played 14 minutes Thursday and went scoreless with 5 rebounds. The show said he was playing about 24 minutes a night early in the season.
Bobby Portis has played 20 minutes or fewer off the bench in recent games after getting about 24 minutes early in the season. The show said Erik Spoelstra has cut his role.
Bones Hyland has taken some minutes from Terrence Shannon Jr. He scored 19 points with eight assists in 20 minutes on October 30.
Bones Hyland has not played more than 20 minutes in any of his last four games, but he scored at least 22.75 DraftKings points in three of them.
Bones Hyland scored 14 points in 13 minutes off the bench Sunday against Utah.
Braden Smith has started Indiana's last two games, playing 42 minutes on November 2 and 24 minutes on Wednesday. The show expects him to keep starting if Kelly Oubre Jr. is out.
Braden Smith started on November 7 but played only 12 minutes, while Kelly Oubre Jr. came off the bench for 16 minutes. The show said it is unclear whether Smith holds onto the starting spot.
Bradley Beal (knee) has not played yet this season and is still recovering.
The show said Branden Carlson or Micah Potter would be Portland's backup center if Robert Williams III sits, not Yang Hansen.

Brandin Podziemski played 37 minutes and had 17 points, eight rebounds and eight assists Sunday against the Clippers without Stephen Curry. The show said Curry's return for the next several games will cut into his and Yaxel Lendeborg's production somewhat.
Brandin Podziemski is playing close to 30 minutes a game or more, and the show said he gains value whenever Stephen Curry misses time.
Podziemski started and had nine points and six rebounds in 32 minutes on Thursday against Miami. The show said his role should stay steady unless injured Warriors return.

Brandon Ingram (heel surgery) and Bradley Beal are out again for the Clippers. Darius Garland is playing through a back issue, and Keaton Wagler has played 25 to 28 minutes off the bench in each of his last three games.
Brandon Ingram missed Sunday's game with his heel injury but is close to making his Clippers debut.
The show said Brandon Miller is running about a 40 percent usage rate and taking close to 30 shots a night. He has scored 24 or more points in five of his last six games.
The show said Brandon Miller's role will take a small hit as Coby White ramps back up. He scored 17 points in 31 minutes Monday.

The show said Miller ranks sixth in the NBA in usage rate and has taken at least 10 threes in all eight games, but he is hitting only about 29% of them. He scored 34, 39 and 31 points in a three-game stretch from Oct. 24 to Oct. 28, but has scored 19, 24 and 17 since.
Brandon Miller played only 26 minutes Wednesday at Brooklyn, down from about 35 a game, and scored 10 points.

The show said Brooklyn doubled Brandon Miller in the season opener and expects aggressive coverage on him Wednesday. It also said Detroit blitzed him on November 2, when he scored 17 points in 31 minutes.

The show said Brandon Miller is out for Monday's game with a hip strain and that no long-term timeline has been announced. He played only 14 minutes in his last game on November 6. Charlotte is running very thin on healthy players.

He is out Monday with a hip strain, Kon Knueppel is out at least four more weeks and Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. Moussa Diabate is questionable, and the show named Hannes Steinbach as the fill-in if he sits.
He had nine points in 17 minutes off the bench Friday against the Lakers. He would likely move into a 26-minute role if Stephen Curry were injured.
The show said Brandon Williams gets more minutes when Stephen Curry sits. When Curry missed Oct. 24, Williams started and scored 20 points in 24 minutes.
Williams played 25 minutes off the bench Sunday with Curry and Green out and scored 17 points. He had played between 14 and 17 minutes in the three games before that.
Williams played 21 minutes Thursday, more than De'Anthony Melton's 17. He had 10 points, 4 assists and 2 blocks.

Brayden Burries has started Milwaukee's last two games, taking Ryan Rollins's starting spot. He had nine points, five rebounds and three assists in 22 minutes on November 4 and has scored at least 20 DraftKings points in four straight games.

Brayden Burries has started at point guard for Milwaukee in each of the last three games, beginning Nov. 2, while Ryan Rollins moved to the bench. On Nov. 6 he played 38 minutes and posted 21 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, and a block. The show said Burries should keep the opportunity as long as he stays a starter, though it expects the production to be uneven like most rookie point guards.
Brayden Burries started again Sunday against Boston and had 13 points, 8 rebounds and 4 assists in 29 minutes.
He has started three straight games at point guard with Ryan Rollins moved to the bench, and he played 38 minutes Friday with 21 points, 11 rebounds and 6 assists.

Brook Lopez started at center for the second straight game on Wednesday and had 20 points, eight rebounds and two blocks in 35 minutes. He played 22 minutes in his previous start, and the show said he fouled out of that game.

Brook Lopez has started the last three Clippers games he played, taking the center spot back from Isaiah Jackson, who has moved to the bench. Lopez played 35 minutes on Nov. 4 and 26 minutes on Nov. 8.
Bryce Hopkins played 28 minutes off the bench with DeMar DeRozan out on Wednesday and had 18 points. The show said Nikola Jokic praised him after the game.
He had 20 points, five rebounds and four assists in 28 minutes Friday against Brooklyn. Detroit pulled its starters late in the win.
Cade Cunningham had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds in 40 minutes Wednesday against Philadelphia.

Cunningham scored only 14 points with 8 assists in 38 minutes against the Lakers on Nov. 8, and the show blamed foul trouble. The show had strong interest in him at $9,500 against Washington on Nov. 9.

Martin started for Dallas on November 6 but played only 11 minutes and scored 0 points. The show called the Dallas frontcourt rotation among Santi Aldama, Daniel Gafford, Morez Johnson Jr. and Martin confusing.

Martin has been starting for Dallas, but he scored 0 points in 11 minutes on Nov. 6 and 2 points in 19 minutes on Nov. 8. The show suggested Santi Aldama could take that starting spot later in the year.
Caleb Wilson played 31 minutes as a starter in a blowout loss and had 23 points with six threes, two blocks and four assists.

He played 34 minutes Monday and scored 24 points with seven rebounds, four steals and four made threes. Box scores show he has played between 31 and 38 minutes in every game, and the show said Chicago keeps him on the floor even in blowouts.
The show said he has taken a large share of Chicago's shots, at about 18 attempts per game. He is averaging 21.2 points in 34 minutes per game.
The show said about 42 percent of Caleb Wilson's shots have come at the rim. Wilson scored 23 points with six threes in 31 minutes on Oct. 30.
Caleb Wilson played only 22 minutes in Wednesday's blowout loss. The show said this was the first blowout in which Chicago cut his minutes.

Caleb Wilson has averaged 32.5 minutes over Chicago's eight games, and the show noted that the Bulls keep giving him big minutes even in blowout losses. His lowest total was 22 minutes in the Nov. 4 game.
The show said Caleb Wilson has a usage rate of about 26 percent, which it said has cut into the usage of everyone else on the Bulls.
Cam Johnson was out on Oct. 28 and is expected to return fairly soon.
Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. are both questionable Saturday against Sacramento. Spencer has moved ahead of Pippen in the rotation and had eight assists in 23 minutes Thursday.
Spencer started on Oct. 31 with Ja Morant out and had 13 assists. In bench games he has played about 19 to 23 minutes with seven or eight assists in his recent outings.
Cam Spencer has seen more playmaking work with Scotty Pippen Jr. out, including 13 assists in a start on October 31. The show said he becomes a strong option whenever Ty Jerome or Pippen misses time.
Cam Spencer had nine assists in 24 minutes off the bench on Wednesday while getting extra backup point guard work with Scotty Pippen Jr. out.

Cam Spencer played 19 minutes off the bench on November 6. The show said he is mainly a fill-in when Ty Jerome sits on back-to-backs, and it said Memphis has its next back-to-back on November 13 and 14.
Cameron Boozer had 8 points, 12 rebounds and 4 assists in 31 minutes. The show said his shooting has been an issue, as it is for many rookies.
He played one minute in a recent game, and the show said the Lakers are still trying to find ways to use him.
Cameron Carr made his debut Sunday and played 1 minute late in the game without scoring.

Cameron Johnson got hurt in the opener and played only 11 minutes on Oct. 22. Since returning he has played 34, 34, and 30 minutes in his first three games back, all starts, and he added 29 minutes with 18 points on Nov. 7. The show said he has the skill set to be Denver's third option behind Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, and it noted he is playing for a new contract.
Cameron Johnson started and scored 18 points with 4 rebounds, a steal and two threes in 29 minutes. The show said he has looked involved since returning from his early-season injury.

Cameron Johnson has started and played 29 to 34 minutes in each of his last four games. He has averaged a little over 12 points in that stretch. The show said he is close to being a must-roster player.
The show said Wallace is presumably out for the season. He has not played since Oct. 25.
Cedric Coward has played in four of Memphis' five games and is averaging about 29 minutes. He has been playing power forward minutes when Cameron Boozer slides to center.
Cedric Coward scored 23 points with nine rebounds, four assists and four steals in 33 minutes on November 4. The show said he took 19 shots, including 12 threes, after several low-volume games.
Johnson started again but had only 2 points and 2 rebounds in 31 minutes.
Chaney Johnson has started Brooklyn's last five games, but he played only nine minutes on Wednesday. The show expects him to start again.
Charles Bassey started Sunday and had 6 points, 10 rebounds, a steal and a block in 20 minutes. The show said he would be worth rostering at 22 to 24 minutes a night.

Charles Bassey played 20 and 23 minutes in Golden State's last two games, but those came with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green out on November 1 and with Al Horford, Brandon Williams and Gui Santos out on November 2. With the roster healthier he played 9, 2 and 2 minutes, and he played only 2 minutes on October 28 when Santos alone was out.
